title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-09-09
content:
Week: 2026-09-02 -> 2026-09-09
Owner: Ethan Brooks
Context: This is the weekly serving-runtime sync focused on kernel optimizations, KV cache correctness/perf, and batching improvements. Mostly status notes from the core kernel and caching subteams plus action items for the coming sprint.

Highlights:
- Kernel: Merged the new fused-attention kernel for small sequence lengths (<=128). Microbenchmarks show 12-18% median latency reduction on A100/80GB for short-response workloads.
- KV cache: Fixed a correctness edge-case that caused rare cache misses when requests were retried with different chunk sizes. Reproduced locally and added a regression test.
- Batching: Rolled out adaptive batch sizing to 10% of traffic in us-west-2; saw 8% token-cost reduction and no measurable P99 latency regressions for conversational workloads.

Metrics & Observations:
- Short seq (<=128) median token latency: -15% on canary GPUs after fused-attn enablement.
- KV cache hit rate on prefix-heavy workloads: stable at ~92% after the retry-fix; previous intermittent dips to 80s resolved.
- Average tokens/second per GPU increased by ~9% with adaptive batching in canary slice.
- P99 latency: unchanged at 150ms for production workload profile; small tail spikes correlated with noisy neighbors on bursty hosts (tracked separately with SRE).

Work completed this week:
- Kernel team: landed fused-attn + perf harness updates; updated dispatcher to prefer fused kernel when seq_len_hist shows >60% short sequences.
- KV team: added deterministic key normalization and latch around prefix eviction that prevented a race during concurrent writes. Added unit + integration tests (kvcache/replay/regression-21).
- Batching: implemented backpressure signal from runtime to router so adaptive batcher reduces batch target under elevated P50 latency. Enabled rollout to 10% in us-west-2.

Blockers / Risks:
- Fused-attn currently has a fallback path that is slower for mid-size sequences (256-512); need to tune kernel heuristics to avoid regressions when traffic mix shifts.
- One of the regression tests for KV cache is flaky in CI on TPU-hosted runners; investigating environment-specific timing assumptions.
- Autoscaler and adaptive batching interaction: when autoscaler triggers scale-down during sustained medium load, batching efficiency drops — potential cost/latency tradeoff for Dedicated customers.

Meeting notes (09/08 tech sync):
- Decision: Enable fused-attn for short sequences in hosted API by default, with an opt-out config in model profile. Rationale: large win for chat assistants; fallback available for mid-seq.
- Action: Priya to add telemetry counters for fused-attn selection decision to pinpoint when mid-seq fallbacks occur in production. Due: 2026-09-16.
- Action: Liam to investigate CI flakiness for kvcache regression test; reproduce in ephemeral env and update test harness to be timing-agnostic. Due: 2026-09-13.
- Action: SRE (Sofia) to run a host-level noisy-neighbor analysis on the P99 tail spikes and propose scheduling constraints for canary fleets. Due: 2026-09-14.

Open questions:
- Should we expand adaptive batching rollout to EU regions next week or wait until autoscaler-batcher interplay is hardened? (ops + product input needed)
- Do we want a hard threshold in the dispatcher for fused-attn (e.g., seq_len_percentile_50 < 140) or a continuous cost-model that scores kernels per request?

Plan for next week:
- Fused-attn: tune mid-seq code path and add more representative medium-length sequences to the perf harness.
- KV cache: stabilize flaky test, add end-to-end replay test for retry scenarios, and monitor production telemetry for any residual misses.
- Batching: monitor adaptive rollout; add an experiment to compare cost-per-token under autoscaler scale-down events (A/B test for Dedicated vs hosted).

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Priya Natarajan: telemetry for fused-attn selection (due 2026-09-16).
- Liam Chen: fix CI flake and update test harness (due 2026-09-13).
- Sofia Martinez / SRE: noisy-neighbor analysis and scheduling recommendations (due 2026-09-14).
- Ethan Brooks: draft rollout notes + customer impact summary for Hosted API opt-in change (due 2026-09-15).

Notes to self / informal:
- Need to sync with product-hosted-api on messaging before defaulting fused-attn; include performance numbers and opt-out instructions in the release notes.
- Keep an eye on Dedicated customers with latency SLOs — adaptive batching/cost wins must not violate SLOs.

Attachments / follow-ups:
- Link to perf dashboards: https://grafana.redwood-infra/company/serving-runtime/fused-attn-canary
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/678
- Jira: SRV-1243 (kvcache-retries)

End of update.
